requirement:
Configuration names MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and be case-sensitive.
Project-selection keys MUST be canonical absolute project-root paths. Model IDs
MUST be nonempty opaque strings, preserving tags and ARNs. `api_key_env` MUST
name a nonempty environment variable without `=` or NUL.

Authoring MUST validate its fields under {cite}`requirements.configuration.loading`.
The `options` map MUST accept backend-defined inference settings rather than a
closed Habeas list; the adapter MUST pass them through Rig's provider parameter
mechanism and report rejection by Rig or the provider. These options MUST NOT
replace the selected model, the assessment prompt, or tool definitions.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Every obligation has marked implementing code and a test that asserts its outcome. I judged from the supplied inputs and did not run any extra searches.

**Obligations, code and tests**

| Obligation | Code | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Configuration names match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and are case-sensitive | `validate_name` (src/config.rs). It is called for `authoring.default`, config names and project-selection config names from `UserAuthoringConfig::validate` and `WorkspaceConfig::validate`. Names are stored and looked up exactly in `resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from`. | `storage_rules_reject_each_invalid_field_with_its_setting` rejects empty, `.`, space, non-ASCII, leading `-` and `_` names. It accepts `Local` and `local` as distinct names, and checks workspace files too. `explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs` shows `DEFAULT` does not resolve to `default`. |
| Project-selection keys are canonical absolute project-root paths | `UserAuthoringConfig::validate` rejects relative paths, `.` and `..` components, non-normalized spellings such as a trailing `/`, and paths that differ from `fs::canonicalize` (symlinks). | The same storage test covers relative, `..`, `./`, trailing-slash and symlink keys. It accepts a canonical existing root and a canonical root that does not exist. |
| Model IDs are nonempty and opaque, preserving tags and ARNs | `BackendConfig::validate` rejects an empty model and otherwise leaves the string untouched. | The storage test rejects an empty model and accepts `name:tag@sha256:abc` and an ARN. `backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults` preserves an ARN. |
| `api_key_env` is nonempty and has no `=` or NUL | `BackendConfig::validate` (Ollama branch). | The storage test rejects `''`, `A=B` and `A\u0000B`, and accepts `MODEL_KEY_1`. |
| Authoring validates its fields under `requirements.configuration.loading` | `UserConfig::parse` and `validate` call `authoring.validate`. `WorkspaceConfig::validate` and `resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from` validate before resolving. Errors name the file and setting. | The storage test asserts that each error contains both the file path and the setting. `invalid_schema_and_feature_values_report_the_configuration_path` also covers this. |
| `options` accepts backend-defined settings with no closed list | `BackendConfig::options`, `options_json` and `OptionValue::validate` accept arbitrary maps. | `backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults` uses arbitrary keys and nested maps. |
| The adapter passes options through Rig's provider parameter mechanism | `RigProvider::complete` sets `request.additional_params` to the remaining options. For Bedrock, `apply_bedrock_options` first maps the native keys. | `ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free` asserts `temperature` and `num_ctx` reach the request body. `bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools` asserts `additionalModelRequestFields` carries `top_k`. `bedrock_native_option_types_are_checked_without_supplying_defaults` also checks that the unrecognized `top_k` option stays in the map. |
| Rejection by Rig or the provider is reported | `complete` maps provider errors through `provider_failure`. `apply_bedrock_options` and `option_type` return typed errors for bad Bedrock option values. | `provider_rejection_of_inference_options_is_reported` covers a provider HTTP 400 whose body appears in stderr, and a Rig-side Bedrock `temperature = 'hot'` error. The unit test in providers.rs covers the type checks. |
| Options MUST NOT replace the model, prompt or tools | `BackendConfig::validate` rejects the keys `model`, `modelId`, `model_id`, `prompt`, `messages`, `system`, `tools`, `tool_choice`, `toolChoice` and `toolConfig`. | The storage test checks each of these keys for both the ollama and bedrock backends. |

**Marking and unspecified behavior**

The implementing and testing items carry `{impl}` and `{test}` references to the subject. The Bedrock native-option mapping and the finite-float check are covered by other requirements that the same code marks (`rig_configuration_mapping`, `configuration_structure`).

text: :::{req} configuration_storage
Configuration names MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and be case-sensitive.
Project-selection keys MUST be canonical absolute project-root paths. Model IDs
MUST be nonempty opaque strings, preserving tags and ARNs. `api_key_env` MUST
name a nonempty environment variable without `=` or NUL.
Authoring MUST validate its fields under {cite}`requirements.configuration.loading`.
The `options` map MUST accept backend-defined inference settings rather than a
closed Habeas list; the adapter MUST pass them through Rig's provider parameter
mechanism and report rejection by Rig or the provider. These options MUST NOT
replace the selected model, the assessment prompt, or tool definitions.
:::{req} loading
An operation MUST load user configuration only when its requirements call for
user settings. A missing user file MUST represent absent user configuration;
whether the operation can proceed MUST be defined by the feature. Loading MUST
NOT create a file, repair malformed input, or supply an undocumented selection.
When loading configuration, Habeas MUST report unreadable files, invalid TOML,
unsupported user-file versions, unknown common keys, and invalid common field
types. It MUST validate the feature sections used by that operation and report
invalid feature settings with the file and setting identified. Unknown keys in
an explicitly documented provider-owned options map MUST follow that feature's
validation rules.
An operation MUST NOT require or semantically validate configuration for a
feature it does not use. This isolation MUST NOT suppress TOML syntax errors in
a shared file that the operation otherwise needs to parse. In particular,
ordinary validation still requires a parseable `book.toml` while remaining
independent of authoring settings and the user configuration file. It MUST apply
the selected workspace's evidence path policy without loading its model clients
or credentials.
